response: {"turns":[{"id":"M1:T21","text":"So just to confirm, at minimum the system has to give reports on actions on cases, organised by case, by user, and in chronological order?"},{"id":"M1:T22","text":"Yes, exactly."},{"id":"M1:T23","text":"Anything else on the audit module?"},{"id":"M1:T24","text":"No, that's it."},{"id":"M1:T25","text":"Okay, let's move to the access module. What do we need there?"},{"id":"M1:T26","text":"The main thing is that security attributes for groups or users, so access rights, security level, privileges, password allocation and management, can only be changed by the super-user. Nobody else."},{"id":"M1:T27","text":"And when a user asks for or searches for a case they don't have rights to, the system should respond in one of three ways, and we pick which one at configuration time. One, show the title and metadata. Two, show that the case exists but not its title or any other metadata. Three, show nothing at all, no hint that it exists. They go up in security in that order. And the third one, the strictest, means those cases can't even show up in the count of search results. That level is normally what you'd use for cases on things like national security."},{"id":"M1:T28","text":"Related to that, for any quick or advanced search, the result list must never include a record the user doesn't have the right to access."},{"id":"M1:T29","text":"Anything more on access?"},{"id":"M1:T30","text":"No, nothing else."},{"id":"M1:T31","text":"Alright, next is ease of use. What are your expectations?"},{"id":"M1:T32","text":"Every error message the system shows has to be meaningful, so the users who are likely to see it can actually act on it. Ideally each one comes with some explanatory text and tells the user what action or actions they can take. And more generally, both the End User and Administrator functions should be easy to use and intuitive throughout."},{"id":"M1:T33","text":"Anything else on ease of use?"},{"id":"M1:T34","text":"No, that covers it."},{"id":"M1:T35","text":"Then let's talk usability. What do you need?"},{"id":"M1:T36","text":"Basically the user interfaces should be designed so they're intuitive for the user."},{"id":"M1:T37","text":"Okay, got it."},{"id":"M1:T38","text":"On the standards side, the user interfaces should comply with ISO 9241. Also, any non-text media, like graphical images or video, should have equivalent text descriptions as an alternative, and/or equivalent text-based functionality."},{"id":"M1:T39","text":"And navigation should be self-descriptive, so users understand where they are, where they've been and where they can go next. ISO 9241-110 gives general guidance on how to get that self-descriptiveness."},{"id":"M1:T40","text":"Right, noted."}]}
